# Siege Mind: results of the pre-registered held-out evaluation

*Generated by experiments/resultsDoc.js from docs/results/*.json. Do not edit by hand; run `npm run results-doc`.*

## What was tested

Siege Mind is a tower defense game whose enemy waves come from one of six modes. **Static** sends fixed, hand-authored waves. **Director v1** and **Director v2** re-weight the enemy types after every wave from what happened to the player's defense (v2 divides by a static baseline and shrinks small samples). The **Random control** changes the composition at random without learning. The **Prior control** applies fixed weights taken only from the static baseline (a lean toward durable enemy types, no learning, no look at the defense). The **Counter arm (reference)** reads the tower loadout directly; it is a reference, not a fair competitor.

All modes spend the same threat per wave and apply the same enemy HP; only the composition of each wave changes.

The players are five scripted bot defenses (balancedR, noLance, noMortar, noPoison, noSniper). The held-out run played 150 held-out seeds x 5 styles x 6 modes = 4500 games, run once (lock run index 1).

## Headline

- Both Directors respond to the player's defense. At wave 9 the weights of Director v1 separate defenses in the predicted direction (contrast 0.19, 95% CI [0.15, 0.22], Holm p < 0.0001) and so do those of Director v2 (0.10, [0.08, 0.11], Holm p < 0.0001). Both confirmatory hypotheses were supported. The informed counter arm, a reference, separates defenses more strongly (0.44).
- Random composition alone did not cost lives. K1 (random minus static, lives lost) was 0.07 ([-0.22, 0.35]) and was not supported. The training seeds had suggested 1.47 ([0.48, 2.45]); that estimate did not replicate.
- Most of Director v1's added difficulty came from a fixed lean toward durable enemy types, not from randomness and not from learning. Of v1's 1.44 extra lives lost against static, the estimate attributes 0.07 to composition variability, 1.63 to the durability bias (a fixed, non-learning arm built from static baselines) and -0.26 to learning on top; the last is small and its sign is not consistent across metrics (see the estimands).
- Director v2 removes that bias: its lives lost and win rate are not detectably different from static (lives lost -0.03 [-0.20, 0.13], win rate 0.000 [-0.018, 0.018]) while its weights still separate defenses (K3).

## Confirmatory results

| ID | Hypothesis | Seeds | Estimate | 95% CI | Holm p | Supported |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| K1 | Composition variability alone (random versus static) costs the player lives | 150 | 0.07 | [-0.22, 0.35] | 0.6522 | no |
| K2 | Director v1 final weights separate defenses in the predicted direction at wave 9 | 124 | 0.19 | [0.15, 0.22] | < 0.0001 | yes |
| K3 | Director v2 weights separate defenses in the predicted direction at wave 9 | 127 | 0.10 | [0.08, 0.11] | < 0.0001 | yes |

Only these three hypotheses are tests. The primary population is the 614 units whose static game reached wave 5; wave 9 was fixed in advance although its coverage (72.6%) was below the registered 75% rule.

The training estimates came from 20 seeds (71 units) and were used to design the confirmatory plan; where they differ from the held-out estimates, the held-out estimates are the ones to report. K1 is the clearest case.

3 of 28 rows have intervals that do not overlap: K1; livesLost: random - static; livesLost: prior - random.

## Limits

- The players are scripted bots on one map; the bots were calibrated on static outcomes and pooled over styles.
- Contrasts at waves 9 and 13 are conditional on survival (coverage at wave 9: 72.6% to 76.4%; at wave 13: 60.3% to 66.6%).
- The coverage rule was not met (minimum coverage at wave 9 is 72.6%, the rule asks for 75%); the registered plan kept wave 9.
- Lives lost saturates because a loss counts as 20.
- The counter arm reads the loadout; it is a reference, not a fair competitor.
- The validation seeds (1021-1030) were not used for confirmation because they are not pristine.
- The secondary metrics show small effects of random composition that the confirmatory family does not cover (final wave, random minus static: -0.21 [-0.33, -0.09]; leaked threat fraction: 0.005 [0.002, 0.008]).
- The wave-5 contrast of Director v1 was much smaller on training data (0.01) than held-out (0.13) and this gap is unexplained beyond sampling variation.

## What this does not show

- That the Director makes the game more enjoyable or better for human players.
- That learning improves difficulty: the learning-on-top estimate is small and mixed in sign.
- That the weights are optimal.
- Anything about human players: none were involved.
